glance.what: Productivity tool that turns screenshots into organized Jira tasks.
glance.why: Cuts manual task entry by reading screenshots automatically.

record.what_it_is: A Chrome extension plus Forge backend that screenshots a Canvas assignment page, has Rovo agents read the assignment details, and creates labeled Jira tasks with due dates automatically.
record.problem_and_user: Students who use Canvas and find it tedious to copy each assignment into a task manager by hand.
record.one_line_pitch: Chrome extension that screenshots Canvas assignment pages and uses Rovo agents via a Forge backend to create labeled Jira tasks automatically.
record.problem_statement: Manually copying assignments into task managers is tedious for students.
record.devpost_tagline: TaskFlow is a smart productivity copilot that turns screenshots into organized Jira tasks, extracting due dates, descriptions, and labels instantly to simplify your workflow.
devpost_first_sections: Manually adding every assignment to task managers was tedious and time-consuming. We wanted a tool that automates this process while adapting to each student’s workflow.

Task Flow AI uses ROVO agents to extract assignment details from screenshots of Canvas pages and automatically creates Jira tasks labeled by class, assignment type, and due date. This reduces repetitive manual input and keeps students organized.

glance.what: AI tool transcribing doctor-patient talks and matching patients to trials.
glance.why: Speeds clinical trial matching from conversations, with HIPAA-compliant privacy.

record.what_it_is: A doctor-patient web platform that transcribes visits by voice, structures and summarizes them, and has agents match the patient to clinical trials; the patient must consent before limited data goes to a trial sponsor.
record.problem_and_user: Trials are under-enrolled because patients do not know they qualify and doctors lack time to screen; targets patients and doctors who also carry note-taking overhead.
record.one_line_pitch: Healthcare app that transcribes doctor-patient visits by voice, summarizes them, and uses agents to match patients to clinical trials with explicit patient consent.
record.problem_statement: Clinical trials go under-enrolled because patients and busy doctors rarely have time to check eligibility during appointments.
record.devpost_tagline: Empowering Doctors, Guiding Patients.
devpost_first_sections: Every year, thousands of clinical trials go under-enrolled, not because patients are unwilling, but because they’re unaware. Doctors often don’t have time to search eligibility criteria or explain options during short appointments, they also have on additional overhead of taking notes of the medical history of patients during the visit. We asked ourselves: What if trial matching could happen automatically in the background during a normal doctor visit? That question led us to build MediBuddy - an autonomous, privacy-first platform that turns doctor-patient conversations into life-saving trial opportunities.

MediBuddy listens to doctor-patient appointments via voice, transcribes the conversation in real-time, structures the medical information, generates a report, and uses autonomous agents to match patients with relevant clinical trials. If a match is found, the patient can securely consent to share limited data with the sponsor all without leaving the app. The platform supports: 📅 Appointment Booking (with doctor approval) 🎙️ Speech-to-text Transcription (via Groq (Whisper v3 Large Turbo)) 🧾 Summarization and Structuring (via Google Gemini) 🧬 Clinical Trial Matching via AI Agents (ASI-1 by Fetch.ai) ✅ Consent Management for trials 🧑‍⚕️ Role-based Dashboards for Doctors and Patients

glance.what: Wearable AR headset and hat rig that visualizes sound for deaf users.
glance.why: Gives deaf people a visual sense of ambient sound they miss.

record.what_it_is: A hat with a four-microphone array wired to a Jetson Orin Nano that classifies sounds, estimates their direction and live-transcribes speech, then shows icons on a radial grid and captions in a Meta Quest 3 AR view for deaf and hard-of-hearing wearers.
record.problem_and_user: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people who miss ambient sounds such as being called, an approaching ambulance or footsteps behind them.
record.one_line_pitch: Hat-mounted mic array plus Jetson Orin Nano that classifies and locates sounds and live-transcribes speech, showing icons and captions in a Meta Quest AR view for deaf users.
record.problem_statement: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people miss the direction and type of surrounding sounds, from everyday cues to danger.
record.devpost_tagline: Audio is a luxury we take for granted, that deaf folks don't get. Ranger is a wearable AR solution aiming to fix that, visualizing audio around them, and bringing them into the world of *sound*.
devpost_first_sections: Sometimes helpful ideas come from the silliest places. One day, as our team was playing Fortnite instead of doing our homework, we realized how helpful it was to have a "sound ring" in game. Noises like enemy footsteps or gunshots are displayed with a visual indicator to show what direction they came from. Luckily, we aren't trapped in Moisty Mire shotgunning ChugJugs, but we did realize people hard of hearing could benefit from this in real life. Both innocuous situations (dropping your wallet in the street and a parent calling you down to dinner) and intense situations (scary noises that would make anyone want to pick up the pace a bit walking home at night, an ambulance screaming by) are

Ranger is an edge-based AR solution for audio visualization that uses a Meta Quest frontend to indicate to the wearer where sounds are coming from. The user wears a hat, which has a microphone array to capture omnidirectional audio and send it to our processing unit, a Jetson Nano. For speech, we live-transcribe conversations using Whisper which allows those hard of hearing to immediately parse what's happening, even if speech comes from behind them. The sound visualization does not interfere with your real-world view, only enhancing the information already available. It's a real-life HUD, enriching the wearer's experience and using edge computing to bring them into the wonderful world of so

glance.for_whom: Satellite operators and space mission planners
glance.why: Protects satellites from debris collisions with on-board AI decisions.

record.devpost_tagline: On-board AI agents autonomously saving satellites from orbital debris.

glance.what: Handwriting-driven digital canvas that interprets writing and intent.
glance.why: Removes button clicks so writing flows naturally.

record.what_it_is: A browser handwriting-notes canvas that interprets pen gestures (underline, box, bracket, strike-through, circle) as formatting commands so the writer never reaches for a toolbar. It also recognizes handwritten math, builds a table of contents and syncs to Google Drive.
record.problem_and_user: Heavy handwritten note-takers, such as students, whose flow breaks when they switch to toolbars to format.
record.one_line_pitch: Handwriting note-taking web app where a TensorFlow.js gesture model turns underlines, boxes and circles into formatting and tool actions.
record.problem_statement: Switching to toolbars interrupts note-taking flow.
record.devpost_tagline: “Write it. Erase it. Shape it. Create it.— no clicks, no limits, just flow. OnePen understands your writing, your intent, and your rhythm — so you can focus on ideas, not buttons.
devpost_first_sections: We’re all heavy note-takers. After trying OneNote, GoodNotes, Notability — we found the same problem: Switching tools breaks the flow. To make a title, highlight, or draw a box, we stop writing, reach for a toolbar, then return — again and again. It’s a small step that, repeated hundreds of times, disrupts thought and creativity. At HackUMass, we realized we shared the same frustration — and the same vision:

OnePen is a handwriting-based note-taking web app that uses AI stroke recognition to let you write, format, and organize without ever touching a toolbar. glance.what: Interactive map of SFU course prerequisites from first year to graduation.
glance.for_whom: SFU students planning their degree path
glance.why: Shows how courses connect so students can plan graduation.

record.what_it_is: A web app that shows SFU course prerequisites as an interactive D3 dependency graph. Searching a course shows its description, prerequisites and equivalents, and Gemini converts messy prerequisite text from SFU course data into structured JSON.
record.problem_and_user: SFU students who find the official goSFU course info unintuitive and must open many course outline pages to trace prerequisites, especially for upper-division courses.
record.one_line_pitch: A web app where searching an SFU course shows an interactive graph of its prerequisites and equivalent courses, extracted with Gemini.
record.problem_statement: Finding SFU course prerequisites means clicking through many outline pages on an unintuitive official system.
record.devpost_tagline: Visualize your journey from first year to graduation.
devpost_first_sections: The idea for SFU Grad Map emerged from our shared frustration with the goSFU system’s outdated and unintuitive design. Many students struggle to find prerequisite information, especially for 200-level and upper-division courses, which often requires manually navigating through multiple course outline pages. We wanted to create a solution that simplifies this process by providing a clear, interactive, and visually engaging way to explore degree progressions.

SFU Grad Map is a web application that allows students to easily visualize their academic journey. By searching for a course, users can instantly see its description, prerequisites, and equivalent courses displayed in a dynamic and interactive graph. This helps students understand course dependencies, plan their future semesters efficiently, and make informed decisions about their academic paths.

glance.what: AI tool explaining what legacy code does, who wrote it, and why.
glance.why: Makes legacy code understandable so teams can maintain it.

record.what_it_is: A developer tool that stores a company's code, commit history and tickets in Snowflake and uses retrieval-augmented generation with Gemini to explain a highlighted legacy snippet as one narrative covering what it does, who changed it, when and why.
record.problem_and_user: Developers and new hires in legacy codebases who lose weeks decoding undocumented fixes and cryptic comments by digging through old commits and tickets.
record.one_line_pitch: Developer tool that stores a company's code, commits and tickets in Snowflake and uses retrieval-augmented generation to explain legacy code as a narrative.
record.problem_statement: Undocumented legacy code with cryptic variables and fixes takes weeks to decode.
record.devpost_tagline: AI-powered code intelligence that reveals what legacy code does, who wrote it, and why it exists. Uses Snowflake, RAG, and Gemini to turn legacy code into clear, maintainable systems.
devpost_first_sections: CommitSense was inspired by our real frustration with legacy code during internships. One teammate spent weeks at a software company trying to decode undocumented fixes and mysterious variables like DONT CHANGE THIS and Magic_Thingy, while the rest of us faced similar onboarding delays in our own roles. We saw how much time and energy were wasted digging through old commits, ticket histories, and scattered comments just to understand why a single line of code existed. These experiences highlighted a clear need for a tool that could instantly explain the purpose, history, and reasoning behind every snippet, sparking our idea to create CommitSense as a way to make onboarding faster and develop

CommitSense is a developer tool that explains legacy code with speed and depth. It stores an entire company’s codebase, commit history, and ticket data in Snowflake, then uses retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to pull precise context for each line of code. This context feeds into the Gemini API, which produces a single clear narrative explaining what the code does, how it works, and why it was written that way. Developers can highlight any snippet to see its full history including who wrote it, when changes occurred, and the reasoning behind every commit, turning scattered documentation into instant actionable insight.

glance.what: Clamp-on guitar device that guides fingers on the fretboard.
glance.why: Gives physical guidance so early guitar practice is easier.

record.what_it_is: A clip-on guitar attachment with laser diodes driven by an ESP32 that lights the fret and string positions of a chord, controlled over Bluetooth from a React web app. The app can read a song sheet with OCR and step through lyrics showing each chord.
record.problem_and_user: Beginner guitar learners who need help memorizing chord fingerings; the device acts as training wheels.
record.one_line_pitch: A clip-on guitar attachment with laser diodes that light chord finger positions, driven by a web app that parses song chords over Bluetooth.
record.problem_statement: Beginners struggle to learn chord finger positions on the fretboard.
record.devpost_tagline: Training wheels for your guitar learning journey
devpost_first_sections: One of our members is an avid guitar player, and the the rest of the group either tried to or have been interested in learning how to play.

FretNot is a clip on attachment to your guitar that projects lasers onto the fretboard to help you learn the finger positionings of chords. It is controlled via a web application that allows the parsing of song lyrics and chords, and can cycle through the song lyrics with their respective chords automatically. The idea is that it's like the training wheel for guitars, where you get the muscle memory in using it which eventually lets you play the chords without it.

record.target_user: rural villagers in Zambia, clinic staff, health logistics planners
record.problem_statement: Rural Zambian villages cannot signal what medicine they need and stock does not reach clinics before rainy-season road closures.
record.devpost_tagline: Three in ten Zambian clinics run out of malaria drugs with a full warehouse. Village pods triage patients and order exactly what’s needed; satellites plan the routes around floods, on real roads.

glance.what: Jetson-powered retrofit kit that makes existing cars self-driving.
glance.why: Adds autonomy to existing cars without buying new vehicles.

record.what_it_is: A retrofit that makes a 2018 Honda Accord drive itself using a Jetson AGX Thor. NVIDIA's Alpamayo R1 reasoning model sets high-level plans and explains them in words, while a sunnypilot-derived control stack and a CAN adapter handle steering and speed. record.target_user: riders and owners of existing cars
record.problem_statement: Self-driving is limited to new vehicles; older cars lack it, and riders get no visibility into an autonomous car's reasoning.
record.devpost_tagline: Turn any car into a self-driving vehicle with the Jetson Thor. Retrofit autonomy, enable rideshare, and deliver smart AI feedback. From real-time reflexes to deep reasoning.
devpost_first_sections: Turn Any Car into a Self-Driving Vehicle Our project is for retrofitting any existing car to make it self-driving. Self-driving should not just be limited to new vehicles, Teslas, and Waymos, but cars bought before self-driving was available too. In our project, we take a 2018 Honda Accord and give it the ability to drive itself using commercially available hardware and open-source software. Using our app, you can request a ride and the car will come to where you are and drive you there.

The central design problem is that driving requires two very different kinds of intelligence. Understanding a scene - recognizing that a pedestrian is about to cross, or that a lane is ending - requires slow, contextual reasoning over visual input. Actually holding a lane and applying the brakes smoothly requires fast, high-frequency control. Trying to do both in a single system forces a tradeoff between intelligence and reaction speed, so we separated them into two layers. glance.why: Lets editors work on one project together, live.

record.problem_and_user: Video editors and creative teams who cannot co-edit one timeline with peers and an AI at the same time.
record.one_line_pitch: Google-Docs-style collaborative video editor, forked from OpenCut, where several editors and a Gemini assistant work on the same timeline in real time via SpacetimeDB.
record.problem_statement: Collaborative video tools exist, but few let humans and AI edit the same project live.
record.devpost_tagline: Collaborating on your video editing projects has never been easier. With CoClip, you can edit in real-time with your peers and AI assistants.

After quickly determining that the idea didn't have a broad enough use case, we pivoted and started looking for a domain where real-time shared state could create a genuinely better experience. After landing on media production, we realized that while collaborative video tools exist, there was still a major gap in editors that allow humans and AI to work together on the same video project in real time . With that, CoClip was born.

CoClip is essentially Google Docs for video editing . With the click of a button, you can share a link with a co-editor and instantly give them access to your timeline, media assets, and project state. Multiple editors can simultaneously work on different parts of the same video without disrupting each other's workflow. glance.what: Web app running a quantum-secured voting tally with candidate setup.
glance.why: Aims to keep votes private while tallies remain verifiable.

record.what_it_is: A quantum-secure electronic voting protocol demo. It applies the GMW multi-party computation scheme with oblivious transfer whose key exchange uses simulated E91 quantum key distribution, plus a simulated zero-knowledge check against double voting, tallying votes without a trusted party.
record.problem_and_user: Election integrity if future quantum computers break classical cryptography; aimed at voters and campaigns needing verifiable, trustless tallies without a blockchain.

record.problem_statement: Future quantum attacks could break classical election cryptography, so vote tallying needs a trustless, verifiable quantum-safe scheme.
record.devpost_tagline: A trustless, quantum-secured vote tallying protocol using Quantum Oblivious Transfer (QOT) with the Ekert-91 (QKD protocol).
devpost_first_sections: The idea of the quantum-secured vote tallying protocol, EleQt , wasn't the first our team came up with. We brainstormed a number of bleeding-edge concepts, from a 'quantum-VQE' first layer for classical neural networks to improved quantum key distribution (QKD) schemas, but always agreed: Our team needs to create an effective project that can be run not far in the future on fault tolerant quantum computers, but right now , in the NISQ era. The original BBCS '2-to-1' protocol involved with OT is meant to be a trustless communication protocol wherein the sender Alice provides two messages, known only to Alice, and the receiver Bob selects one of the two messages, the selection of which is known only to Bob. glance.what: Texting assistant that handles moving logistics, from apartments to bills.
glance.why: Moving tasks sprawl across sites and people; Elfie coordinates them.

glance.for_whom: Grant seekers applying to government programs

record.problem_and_user: Farmers who cannot find funding they qualify for; existing tools have stale data and no application guidance.
record.one_line_pitch: Scrapes government funding programs, matches farmers to them in natural language, and drafts application plans with auto-filled PDF forms.

One of our team members has seen firsthand how healthy and edible produce gets discarded just because it doesn’t look perfect. This issue is REAL and needs to be addressed immediately

If you complete the task on time, you get your ETH back. But if you miss the deadline, your ETH is donated to a charity of your choice. TaskChain turns your goals into meaningful actions, incentivizing productivity while making a positive impact on the world.

record.problem_and_user: UMD students whose small eco-friendly choices go unnoticed and unrewarded.

record.problem_statement: Students want to be sustainable but have no engaging way to track and be rewarded for small daily eco actions.

devpost_first_sections: We were inspired by a simple problem: people want to be environmentally sustainable , but there’s no easy, engaging way to track and feel rewarded for those actions in daily life. At a campus like UMD , students make small decisions every day—walking instead of driving, recycling, conserving energy—but those actions often go unnoticed. We wanted to turn sustainability into something visible, interactive, and motivating —like a game. By combining AI , real-world behavior tracking , and a virtual companion , EcoBuddy was born.

EcoBuddy is an AI-powered sustainability companion that: Lets users log eco-friendly actions through voice or text Uses image verification to confirm real-world actions Assigns a sustainability score based on user behavior Evolves a virtual “Terp Turtle” buddy as users level up Rewards users with real incentives like dining credits and promo codes The more sustainable you are, the more your buddy grows—and the more rewards you unlock.

devpost_first_sections: Campus dining is confusing, unpredictable, and rarely health-friendly. Students with allergies, athletes, and people with chronic conditions struggle to know what’s safe or good for them. We wanted to fix that.

ByteBite analyzes dining-hall menus and generates personalized meal recommendations, allergy alerts, and wellness-optimized options. It supports diabetic, low-sodium, and high-protein modes, plus mood-based tracking and a gamified health avatar.

We were also excited by the Fetch.ai Agentverse track and wanted to prove that a multi-agent architecture could coordinate real spatial reasoning, not just chat responses.

devpost_first_sections: As curious college students, we set out to create an engaging way to explore how images relate to one another. Atlas visualizes image relationships in 3D. We map images by semantic similarity using CLIP embeddings, then project them to 3D with PCA . Similar images cluster together, making it easier to explore and understand visual relationships.

Atlas is a 3D neural map of visual space that: Uploads images and generates CLIP embeddings (512‑D). Projects embeddings to 3D using PCA Clusters images with K‑means (optimal k via silhouette score). glance.why: Cuts costs by automating maintenance and energy monitoring.

record.what_it_is: A concept dashboard for businesses to monitor energy use, detect waste and automatically schedule HVAC and maintenance using sensor feedback and machine learning; repo is a small React app.
record.problem_and_user: Business owners and facilities teams losing money on inefficient energy use; cites $370 billion annual US energy waste and a restaurant losing $3,000-5,000 monthly on air conditioning.
record.one_line_pitch: Energy-management tool for businesses that tracks consumption from sensors, flags inefficiencies and schedules HVAC and maintenance.
record.target_user: small business owners such as restaurants
record.problem_statement: Small businesses overspend on energy and lack tools to spot waste and plan maintenance.
record.devpost_tagline: An app that empowers facilities to automate maintenance scheduling, track customer feedback, monitor energy usage, and helping businesses reduce costs. Potentially saving $111 billion in the US.
devpost_first_sections: UtiliTrack was inspired by a friend’s struggle to manage energy costs in his family-run restaurant. During peak summer months, he was losing between $3,000 to $5,000 monthly just on air conditioning. The toll on his business was severe—not only in expenses but also in wear and tear, leading to vent leaks and damage. His experience opened our eyes to the widespread infrastructure inefficiencies many businesses face. With an annual $370 billion energy waste in the U.S., we set out to create a solution to combat this issue.

UtiliTrack provides businesses with a powerful tool to manage energy usage and streamline maintenance. It continuously monitors energy consumption patterns and detects inefficiencies, allowing systems like HVAC to operate only when necessary. By integrating automated scheduling and sensor feedback, UtiliTrack adjusts power usage dynamically. This solution not only saves costs but also reduces the strain on equipment, which means less frequent breakdowns. Businesses can now manage operational efficiency from a single dashboard, reducing waste and boosting customer satisfaction.

Studies show that people miss out on millions in rewards because they don’t optimize card usage. We wanted to solve this problem in a way that’s effortless — no manual lookups, no entering merchants. That’s how Crediwise was born: a Chrome extension that’s always there at checkout, making sure you swipe smart and save more.

Auto-detects checkout pages across domains (Amazon, Spotify, Delta, etc.). Instantly recommends the best card to maximize rewards/cashback, factoring in base rates and public offers. Provides a savings summary dashboard: How much you’ve saved so far, What other cards would have offered, Category breakdowns and overall performance Tracks lifetime savings and generates AI-powered insights about spending patterns.

devpost_first_sections: Airwaves is a rhythm-based browser game that uses your webcam to detect hand movements and translate them into mouse clicks, scrolls, and gestures. devpost_first_sections: Depth perception is the bottleneck for almost every embodied AI system — robots, AR headsets, accessibility tools, autonomous vehicles. And yet the depth-sensor market is bizarrely bimodal: an industrial Velodyne or Ouster will run you $8,000–$75,000, while the solid-state LiDAR Apple ships in every iPhone Pro since 2020 is $3–$25 in component cost. Same physics, three orders of magnitude in price. The catch is that the iPhone's depth output is sparse — a 192×256 map with a per-pixel confidence flag — and at full camera resolution it looks like a smear. The hardware gap closed years ago; the software gap never did. Plain bicubic upsampling gets you to camera resolution but ignores the RGB im

SPECTRA turns the iPhone Pro's sparse 192×256 LiDAR signal into a dense 768×1024 metric depth map, in real time, on-device. It has two halves: SPECTRANet — an RGB-guided depth upsampler. The output is metrically faithful but follows real surface boundaries instead of smearing across them. SPECTRALive — a SwiftUI/ARKit iOS app with three modes: Live Depth (raw LiDAR colormap overlay), SPECTRANet (our enhanced depth, on-device via CoreML or remote via an ASUS Ascent GX10 server), and Demo (A/B side-by-side). You can capture and share RGB+depth composites straight from the shutter.

glance.what: Gesture-controlled drawing app where your hands act as brushes.
glance.why: Lets people paint in the air with no tools needed.

record.what_it_is: A Python desktop drawing game controlled by hand gestures from a webcam: a closed fist draws, an open hand stops. In single-player the Gemini model guesses the drawing; in multiplayer it judges whose drawing is clearest.
record.problem_and_user: Casual players of all ages, and those who struggle with keyboards or mice, who want a gesture-based interface.
record.one_line_pitch: Drawing and guessing game controlled by webcam hand gestures where a Gemini model guesses the sketch.
record.problem_statement: Wanted a playful gesture-driven game inspired by fiction, replacing mouse input with hand tracking.
record.devpost_tagline: Jesture is a magical gesture-based drawing experience where your hands become the paintbrush! Wave your arms about and watch your beautiful (or hilariously terrible) art manifest on your screen!
devpost_first_sections: The inspiration for Jesture mainly comes from popular fiction. The idea started as one one-off comment by a couple of my friends who thought it would be interesting to be able to control your computer through hand gestures like in Iron Man, where Tony Stark uses hand gestures to control devices or interact with virtual environments. This concept felt futuristic and exciting, but we also saw a practical application: making technology more accessible and intuitive. Gesture-based controls can provide an alternative interface for individuals with limited mobility or those who find traditional input devices like keyboards and mice challenging to use. By combining creativity and accessibility, we

Jesture is an interactive drawing and guessing game powered by gesture recognition. Users can draw on a virtual canvas using hand gestures, switch between drawing modes (free draw, line, circle), and have an AI guess what they are drawing. It combines creativity, technology, and fun into one seamless package.

glance.what: Live social-sentiment dashboard scoring stocks by online buzz.
glance.why: Surfaces sentiment shifts to inform investment decisions.

record.problem_and_user: Stock and crypto traders who find manually tracking social chatter impractical.
record.one_line_pitch: Dashboard that scans social media for keywords tied to chosen stocks and crypto, runs NLP sentiment analysis and aggregates signals in real time.
record.problem_statement: Investors cannot track social sentiment across platforms quickly enough to use it.
record.devpost_tagline: Real-Time Sentiment, Smarter Insights.
devpost_first_sections: When people participate in stock market, it's always important to focus on social sentiment. With chatter on social platforms reflecting markets more than ever, we were inspired to create a tool that translates this vast, real-time data into actionable insights for smarter financial decision-making.

TrendPulse scans multiple social media channels for relevant keywords related to user's preferences for stocks and cryptocurrencies. By leveraging advanced NLP models, it analyzes posts for sentiment, aggregating data to produce a real-time market trend and risk index that helps users gauge market mood and make informed decisions.

glance.what: Desktop circuit generator producing circuits from text requests.
glance.why: Helps students build and test circuits in a virtual lab.

record.what_it_is: A Unity virtual-reality electronics simulator for Meta Quest where users place components, wires and ICs on a virtual breadboard and see circuit behavior simulated. The repo adds a natural-language circuit command generator and a 2D Pygame circuit tester.
record.problem_and_user: Beginners and educators for whom physical breadboarding is intimidating and needs real components that can be damaged.
record.one_line_pitch: Unity VR virtual breadboard where users place components and wire circuits to learn electronics hands-on.
record.problem_statement: Learning circuit design needs physical parts and lab access; a VR breadboard makes practice accessible and safe.
record.devpost_tagline: Interactive VR based realistic breadboard, wires, and components for students to build and test circuits in an engaging, risk-free virtual lab, with a Meta Quest 3.
devpost_first_sections: As technology enthusiasts and educators, we recognize the importance of hands-on learning in electronics and circuit design. However, traditional breadboarding can be intimidating for beginners and requires physical components. We wanted to create an accessible, immersive, and risk-free environment for learners to explore and experiment with circuits. This led us to develop Circuit Simulator, a VR application that brings the electronics lab experience to virtual reality. 🎮🔌

Circuit Simulator provides a fully interactive virtual breadboard where users can build, test, and learn about electronic circuits. With realistic wires and functioning IC units, users can construct complex circuits and observe their behavior in real-time. The application offers a hands-on learning experience without the need for physical components or the risk of damaging equipment. 🧪🔧

glance.what: Stock trading sandbox game where players battle other traders.
glance.why: Lets people practice trading without risking real money.

record.what_it_is: A Flask web app where users build simulated stock portfolios from S&P 500 stocks using real market data, view performance graphs and metrics with explanatory pop-ups, and compare with friends in leagues.
record.problem_and_user: Everyday people intimidated by financial jargon, and would-be traders who cannot afford to trade, wanting to learn and compete without real money.
record.one_line_pitch: Web app for simulated S&P 500 stock portfolios using real market data, with graphs, metrics and friend leagues to make investing less intimidating.
record.problem_statement: Financial jargon, calculations and visualizations intimidate everyday people trying to learn about investing.
record.devpost_tagline: Have you ever wanted to trade stocks, but don't have the money to do so? Perhaps, maybe you want to battle it out against fellow traders? Market Melee is the perfect stock sandbox for you!
devpost_first_sections: Our inspiration for Market Melee stemmed from the entire group taking an Introduction to Computational Investing class. After seeing how a lot of financial jargon, calculations, and visualizations are intimidating to the everyday person, we decided to build Market Melee to make stock market investing more accessible and engaging for everyone. By gamifying the investing experience, we aimed to create a platform where any user can learn, compete, and grow their financial knowledge in a fun environment.

Market Melee is a web application that allows users to create and manage simulated stock portfolios using real-time market data. Having hundreds of stocks to choose from, notably from the S&P 500, they are able to allocate their investments and track their portfolio performance over time. Features include interactive graphs, detailed stock metrics, and a place to track your own progress against friends within your league.

glance.what: Restaurant swipe app matching diners to places by description.
glance.for_whom: Diners who can't decide where to eat
glance.why: Ends food indecision by swiping on tailored restaurant picks.

record.what_it_is: A 'Tinder for restaurants' web app: describe what you crave in plain English, an LLM converts it into Yelp search filters, then you swipe through full-screen restaurant cards to find a match.
record.problem_and_user: Groups and individuals suffering decision fatigue over where to eat; Yelp and Maps are information-dense but slow for deciding.
record.one_line_pitch: Restaurant finder where an LLM turns a plain-English request into Yelp searches and users swipe poster-style cards, ranked by a weighted score.
record.target_user: groups and couples choosing where to eat
record.problem_statement: Groups suffer decision fatigue picking dinner, and Yelp or Google Maps give too much information to decide quickly.
record.devpost_tagline: Tinder, but for food — describe what you want, swipe through restaurants, and instantly match with the perfect place to eat.
devpost_first_sections: Love At First Bite

We've all been there: it's Friday night, you're hungry, and the group chat spirals into "I don't know, where do you want to go?" followed by "You pick." Decision fatigue is real. Existing apps like Yelp and Google Maps excel at information density, but they're terrible at helping groups make quick decisions. We realized that the swipe mechanic—proven effective by dating apps—is fundamentally the fastest way to make binary choices. We built Love At First Bite to make finding dinner faster and more fun than the traditional restaurant browsing experience.
